ety.text: From Proto-Italic *mi(k)skō (“to mix”), from Proto-Indo-European *miḱ-sḱé-, inchoative present of *meyǵ-, *meyḱ- (“to mix”). The second conjugation of this verb is unexplained. It is possible that the original third-conjugation form of the verb is continued by Praenestine misc. The u-perfect of this verb is also unusual; it may have replaced an earlier form *misxī.
